text:
# file: .github/workflows/examples.yml (yml, 79 lines)
name: Regenerate real-world examples

# Manual only (see docs/benchmarks.md "CI tiers"): every one of the five
# repositories in examples/repositories.yaml moves upstream, so an automatic
# schedule would mean either constant no-op noise or a workflow silently
# committing whatever changed on someone else's main branch. This runs only
# when a maintainer asks for it, and never commits by itself — it uploads the
# regenerated examples/ and benchmarks/results.json as an artifact for a human
# to review and open as a PR.
on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      repo:
        description: "Registry id from examples/repositories.yaml, or 'all'"
        required: true
        default: "django"

concurrency:
  # Manual, long (five upstream clones), and writes an artifact: queue a second
  # dispatch behind the first rather than cancelling work already paid for.
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  PYTHONUNBUFFERED: "1"
  FORCE_COLOR: "1"

jobs:
  regenerate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1  # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97  # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
          cache: pip

      - run: pip install -e "." pyyaml

      - name: Generate
        shell: bash
        env:
          INPUT_REPO: ${{ inputs.repo }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ "$INPUT_REPO" = "all" ]; then
            python scripts/generate_examples.py --all
          else
            python scripts/generate_examples.py --repo "$INPUT_REPO"
          fi

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a  # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: regenerated-examples
          path: |
            examples/
            benchmarks/results.json
          retention-days: 14

      - name: Generate Examples Step Summary
        if: always()
        shell: bash
        env:
          INPUT_REPO: ${{ inputs.repo }}
        run: |
          cat << EOF >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          ### 📁 Regenerate Real-World Examples Summary

          - **Target Repository**: \`$INPUT_REPO\`
          - **Artifact Generated**: \`regenerated-examples\` (retained for 14 days)
          EOF

name: index-repo.yml
text:
# file: .github/workflows/index-repo.yml (yml, 85 lines)
name: Index repository
on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      repo:
        description: "Target repo: owner/repo or a GitHub URL"
        required: true
      ref:
        description: "Branch or tag (blank = default branch)"
        required: false
        default: ""
      git_history:
        description: "Commits to scan for CO_CHANGE edges (0 = skip)"
        required: false
        default: "200"
      formats:
        description: "Comma list: jsonl,graphml,cypher,overview,html"
        required: false
        default: "jsonl,graphml,cypher,overview,html"
      exclude:
        description: "Space-separated globs to exclude, e.g. '**/test/**'"
        required: false
        default: ""
      publish_release:
        description: "Also attach the graph to a GitHub Release in this repo"
        type: boolean
        required: false
        default: false

concurrency:
  # Per target repository, so indexing two different repos stays parallel while
  # a repeat dispatch for the same one queues.
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ inputs.repo }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: write

jobs:
  index:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    steps:
      - name: Check out repo2graph
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1  # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Compute slug
        id: slug
        env:
          R2G_REPO: ${{ inputs.repo }}
        run: |
          slug="$(printf '%s' "$R2G_REPO" | sed -E 's#.*github\.com[:/]##; s#\.git/?$##; s#/#__#g')"
          echo "slug=$slug" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Build graph
        id: build
        uses: ./
        with:
          repo: ${{ inputs.repo }}
          ref: ${{ inputs.ref }}
          out: out/${{ steps.slug.outputs.slug }}
          git-history: ${{ inputs.git_history }}
          formats: ${{ inputs.formats }}
          exclude: ${{ inputs.exclude }}
          artifact-name: graph-${{ steps.slug.outputs.slug }}
          token: ${{ secrets.TARGET_REPO_TOKEN || github.token }}

      - name: Attach graph to a release
        if: ${{ inputs.publish_release }}
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          R2G_REPO: ${{ inputs.repo }}
          R2G_SLUG: ${{ steps.slug.outputs.slug }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          slug="$R2G_SLUG"
          tag="graph-$slug-$(date -u +%Y%m%d%H%M%S)"
          (cd out && zip -qr "$slug.zip" "$slug")
          notes=(--notes "Graph artifacts for $R2G_REPO")
          if [ -f "out/$slug/human/overview.md" ]; then notes=(--notes-file "out/$slug/human/overview.md"); fi
          gh release create "$tag" "out/$slug.zip" \
            --title "Graph: $R2G_REPO" "${notes[@]}"

name: lockfile.yml
text:
# file: .github/workflows/lockfile.yml (yml, 113 lines)
name: Lockfile Sync

# Automatically verifies that uv.lock is up to date with pyproject.toml.
# When a pull request touches pyproject.toml without updating uv.lock, this
# workflow detects the discrepancy, generates the updated lockfile, and uploads
# it as a CI artifact so contributors and maintainers can easily retrieve it.
# On manual workflow_dispatch, it can automatically commit the fix back to the branch.
on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - "pyproject.toml"
      - "uv.lock"
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      auto_commit:
        description: "Automatically commit updated uv.lock back to branch"
        type: boolean
        default: false

concurrency:
  # Cancel only the pull_request runs, which are pure checks and where a newer
  # push makes the older one redundant. A workflow_dispatch run can reach the
  # auto_commit step and `git push`, so those queue instead: the two event
  # types already land in different groups (head_ref vs ref), so this only
  # affects a second dispatch racing the first.
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.head_ref || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  PYTHONUNBUFFERED: "1"
  FORCE_COLOR: "1"

jobs:
  check-lockfile:
    name: Lockfile Freshness
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      # `contents: write` is for the dispatch-only auto-commit step's `git push`
      # at the end of this job. No step in this file uses the pull-requests
      # scope -- it neither comments, labels, nor opens anything -- so it is not
      # requested.
      contents: write
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1  # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.head_ref || github.ref }}
          # Persist the token *only* on the dispatch path that actually pushes.
          # On the `pull_request` path this job runs `uv lock`, which builds an
          # sdist for any dependency without a wheel -- i.e. it executes build
          # backend code influenced by the PR's own pyproject.toml. Holding a
          # write-scoped credential in the same job while that runs is blast
          # radius with no purpose, since that path never pushes. The
          # `github.event.inputs` string comparison mirrors the auto-commit
          # step's own `if:` below, so both gates open on exactly the same input.
          persist-credentials: ${{ github.event.inputs.auto_commit == 'true' }}

      - name: Set up Python 3.12
        uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97  # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"

      - name: Install uv
        run: pip install uv

      - name: Check uv.lock freshness
        id: check
        run: |
          if uv lock --check; then
            echo "status=ok" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "uv.lock is in sync with pyproject.toml."
          else
            echo "status=stale" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::error title=Stale uv.lock::uv.lock is out of sync with pyproject.toml. Please run 'uv lock' and commit the updated uv.lock file."
            uv lock
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Generate Lockfile Freshness Step Summary
        if: always()
        shell: bash
        run: |
          cat << EOF >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          ### 🔒 Lockfile Synchronization Summary

          | Property | Status |
          | :--- | :--- |
          | **Freshness Check** | ${{ steps.check.outputs.status == 'ok' && '✅ In sync with pyproject.toml' || '❌ Out of sync' }} |
          | **Trigger Event** | \`${{ github.event_name }}\` |
          EOF

      - name: Upload updated uv.lock as artifact
        if: failure() && steps.check.outputs.status == 'stale'
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a  # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: uv.lock-updated
          path: uv.lock
          if-no-files-found: ignore

        run: |
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          git add uv.lock
          git commit -m "chore(deps): update uv.lock to match pyproject.toml"
          git push

name: pr-impact.yml
text:
# file: .github/workflows/pr-impact.yml (yml, 187 lines)
name: "PR Architectural Impact Analysis"

# Posts the architectural blast radius of a pull request as prod-igy, the
# repository's PR assistant -- the same identity that posts the triage comment,
# so a contributor sees one bot account rather than two.
#
# Two things about this job are load-bearing and easy to undo:
#
# 1. The index is built on the *head* commit being analyzed, never on the base
#    ref. `repo2graph impact` intersects diff hunks (head-side line numbers)
#    with symbol spans read out of the index, and resolves callers, tests and
#    imports through that index. An index built on the base cannot contain a
#    file the PR adds, and its line numbers belong to a different version of
#    every file the PR touches -- so added files read as unreachable orphans and
#    modified symbols resolve against the wrong lines. That produced three
#    code-scanning alerts on PR #422 naming perfectly ordinary edits, and none of
#    them were visible as an error: the run stayed green and the numbers looked
#    plausible. `guardrails.stale_index_notice` now says so out loud when it
#    happens, but the fix is to build here, on the head tree.
#
# 2. The prod-igy App key is minted only for a pull request from a branch of
#    this repository. This job runs `pip install .` from the PR head, so on a
#    fork PR the App key would be handed to a job that has already executed
#    contributor-authored build code. A fork PR still gets the full analysis in
#    the job summary and the uploaded artifact -- the comment and the SARIF
#    upload are what GitHub already withholds there, because `GITHUB_TOKEN` is
#    read-only for fork pull requests regardless of the `permissions:` block.
on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]
    paths-ignore:
      - "docs/**"
      - "*.md"

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  # One analysis per PR. Cancelling is safe here, unlike prod-igy's triage: this
  # job answers a push, never a human, and a superseded push's report is stale
  # by definition -- the comment it would edit is the one the new run rewrites.
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  impact:
    name: "Analyze Diff Impact"
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
      # A PR conversation comment goes through the issue-comment endpoints, which
      # accept `pull-requests: write` when the issue is a pull request. No
      # `issues: write` needed, for GITHUB_TOKEN or for the App token below.
      pull-requests: write
      security-events: write
    env:
      # Job-level, for the same reason prod-igy.yml promoted its probes here
      # (#375): every step's `if:` and `env:` then reads one resolved value.
      SAME_REPO: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository }}
      HAS_APP_ID: ${{ secrets.PRODIGY_APP_ID }}
      HAS_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.PRODIGY_PRIVATE_KEY }}
    steps:
      # fetch-depth: 0 so `origin/<base>` exists for the three-dot diff. For a
      # pull_request event this leaves HEAD at the merge commit, which is the
      # tree that will actually land -- so that is what gets indexed.
      - name: "Checkout PR merge commit"
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: "Set up Python"
        uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
          cache: "pip"

      - name: "Install repo2graph"
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip
          pip install .

      - name: "Build graph index on the analyzed head tree"
        run: repo2graph build . -o .repo2graph-head --formats jsonl,overview

      - name: "Run repo2graph impact analysis"
        id: impact
        env:
          BASE_REF: ${{ github.base_ref }}

name: pr-impact.yml
text:
# file: .github/workflows/pr-impact.yml (yml, 187 lines)

      - name: "Build graph index on the analyzed head tree"
        run: repo2graph build . -o .repo2graph-head --formats jsonl,overview

      - name: "Run repo2graph impact analysis"
        id: impact
        env:
          BASE_REF: ${{ github.base_ref }}
        run: |
          mkdir -p impact-reports
          run_impact() {
            repo2graph impact -i .repo2graph-head \
              --base "origin/$BASE_REF" --head HEAD \
              --format "$1" --write "impact-reports/$2"
          }
          run_impact markdown   impact-report.md
          run_impact json       impact-report.json
          run_impact sarif      impact-report.sarif
          run_impact pr-comment pr-comment.md

      - name: "Publish job summary"
        run: cat impact-reports/pr-comment.md >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      - name: "Upload impact artifacts"
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: pr-impact-analysis
          path: impact-reports/
          retention-days: 14

      # continue-on-error: a fork pull request gets a read-only GITHUB_TOKEN, so
      # this upload is rejected there and must not fail the analysis.
      - name: "Upload SARIF results to GitHub code scanning"
        uses: github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@2892aa5e19bbd11bc0cff5427e3b750a04d9e3c2 # v4.38.2
        continue-on-error: true
        with:
          sarif_file: impact-reports/impact-report.sarif
          category: repo2graph-impact

      # continue-on-error: the analysis is the deliverable. A revoked key, a
      # changed App grant or an API blip degrades the comment to the
      # github-actions[bot] fallback the next step reports -- it must not turn a
      # completed impact report into a red check.
      - name: "Generate prod-igy token"
        id: app-token
        if: ${{ env.SAME_REPO == 'true' && env.HAS_APP_ID != '' && env.HAS_PRIVATE_KEY != '' }}
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.PRODIGY_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.PRODIGY_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          # Scope the minted token down from the App installation's full grant to
          # exactly what the comment step below does -- an app token otherwise
          # inherits every permission the installation holds.
          #
          # Request *only* permissions the installation actually grants:
          # `permission-*` asks for that exact set and the API rejects the whole
          # request with 422 "The permissions requested are not granted to this
          # installation" if any one entry is absent, so a well-meant extra mints
          # nothing at all and the comment silently posts as github-actions[bot].
          # prod-igy is installed with pull_requests: write, contents: read and
          # metadata: read -- not issues, not checks (probed one permission per
          # token request, actions/runs/36200243473). `pull_requests: write` is
          # what the issue-comment endpoints below need for a pull request.
          permission-pull-requests: write

      # Without this the GITHUB_TOKEN fallback is invisible: a revoked App key
      # means the comment silently posts as github-actions[bot] again.
      - name: "Report posting identity"
        if: ${{ env.SAME_REPO == 'true' }}
        env:
          APP_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
        run: |
          if [ -n "$APP_TOKEN" ]; then
            echo "::notice::impact analysis is posting as prod-igy (GitHub App installation token)"
          else
            echo "::notice::impact analysis is posting as github-actions[bot] (GITHUB_TOKEN fallback: no App credentials configured or token generation failed)"
          fi

      # Upsert, not append. The marker is repo2graph.impact.PR_COMMENT_MARKER,
      # which format_pr_comment writes as the comment's first line;
      # tests/test_pr_impact.py pins the two spellings against each other.

          else
            echo "::notice::impact analysis is posting as github-actions[bot] (GITHUB_TOKEN fallback: no App credentials configured or token generation failed)"
          fi

      # Upsert, not append. The marker is repo2graph.impact.PR_COMMENT_MARKER,
      # which format_pr_comment writes as the comment's first line;
      # tests/test_pr_impact.py pins the two spellings against each other.
      - name: "Post or update the prod-igy impact comment"
        if: ${{ env.SAME_REPO == 'true' }}
        continue-on-error: true
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
        run: |
          existing=$(gh api --paginate "repos/$GH_REPO/issues/$PR_NUMBER/comments" \
            --jq '[.[] | select(.body | startswith("<!-- repo2graph-impact-comment -->")) | .id] | last // empty')

          # -Rs: the whole file as one JSON string, so no amount of Markdown,
          # backtick or quote in the report can break out of the request body.
          jq -Rs '{body: .}' < impact-reports/pr-comment.md > comment-body.json

          if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
            gh api -X PATCH "repos/$GH_REPO/issues/comments/$existing" --input comment-body.json >/dev/null
            echo "::notice::updated impact comment $existing"
          else
            gh api -X POST "repos/$GH_REPO/issues/$PR_NUMBER/comments" --input comment-body.json >/dev/null
            echo "::notice::posted a new impact comment on PR $PR_NUMBER"
          fi

name: prod-igy.yml
text:
# file: .github/workflows/prod-igy.yml (yml, 196 lines)
name: prod-igy

# Automated PR assistant for repo2graph:
# - Classifies PRs and assigns type, size, area, and status labels
# - Analyzes base branch alignment, commit divergence, and linked issues
# - Reminds and tags PR authors if their branch is behind base or has merge conflicts
# - Surfaces repository-specific architecture and review reminders from AGENTS.md
# - Reports check-run results for the PR head
# - Adds a plain-language description of the diff and a title suggestion
#
# The summary step is shown the diff and nothing else. It does not review the
# change, does not look at the rest of the codebase, and does not assign labels
# -- labels stay path- and size-derived. There is no contributor-facing entry
# point to it: it fires only on the events below, takes no instruction from the
# pull request, and cannot run more than PRODIGY_AI_MAX_RUNS_PER_PR times.
'on':
  # `edited` deliberately absent: it fires whenever a PR's title or body
  # changes, which the author controls (including a fork author) and can
  # pull at will. The job holds pull-requests: write, issues: write and an
  # API key, so a trigger the author can re-fire on demand is model spend
  # and API surface the author rate-controls, not this workflow. `opened`,
  # `synchronize` and `reopened` are unaffected.
  pull_request_target:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      pr_number:
        description: "PR number to inspect (leave blank or 'all' to inspect all open PRs)"
        required: false
        default: "all"
  issue_comment:
    types: [created]

concurrency:
  # Serialise per PR/issue, but do not cancel. Two triage runs racing on one PR
  # is the failure mode to avoid, and the group alone prevents that. Cancelling
  # would also reach the `issue_comment` trigger, where a run is answering a
  # human who typed `@prod-igy`: a `synchronize` arriving a moment later would
  # kill that reply and the comment would never be posted.
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.event.issue.number || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

# Top-level default: read-only
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  triage:
    name: PR Triage & Inspection
    if: |
      github.event_name == 'pull_request_target' ||
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||
      (github.event_name == 'issue_comment' && github.event.issue.pull_request &&
       (contains(github.event.comment.body, '@prod-igy') || contains(github.event.comment.body, '/prod-igy')) &&
       (github.event.comment.author_association == 'OWNER' ||
        github.event.comment.author_association == 'MEMBER' ||
        github.event.comment.author_association == 'COLLABORATOR'))
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: write
      issues: write
      checks: read  # check-run results for the PR head
    env:
      # Promoted from the app-token step's own `env:` (#375): that step's
      # `if:` read these from a block declared on the same step, which works
      # but depends on evaluation-order behaviour GitHub documents loosely.
      # A job-level env removes the question -- every step's `if:` and `env:`
      # sees the same resolved value, in the same context expressions always
      # use for job-level env.
      HAS_APP_ID: ${{ secrets.PRODIGY_APP_ID }}
      HAS_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.PRODIGY_PRIVATE_KEY }}
      # Same promotion, for the same reason, applied to the one step #375
      # missed: "Install Anthropic SDK" gated on `env.PRODIGY_AI` while
      # declaring `PRODIGY_AI` in that same step's own `env:` block. A step's
      # `env:` is not in scope for that step's `if:`, so the gate read an empty
      # string and never opened -- the SDK was never installed even with
      # `vars.PRODIGY_AI` set to `true`, and because the step is
      # `continue-on-error` the script just fell back to its deterministic
      # inspection. Silent, and invisible in any run where the var is unset.

name: prod-igy.yml
text:
# file: .github/workflows/prod-igy.yml (yml, 196 lines)
      # Same promotion, for the same reason, applied to the one step #375
      # missed: "Install Anthropic SDK" gated on `env.PRODIGY_AI` while
      # declaring `PRODIGY_AI` in that same step's own `env:` block. A step's
      # `env:` is not in scope for that step's `if:`, so the gate read an empty
      # string and never opened -- the SDK was never installed even with
      # `vars.PRODIGY_AI` set to `true`, and because the step is
      # `continue-on-error` the script just fell back to its deterministic
      # inspection. Silent, and invisible in any run where the var is unset.
      PRODIGY_AI: ${{ vars.PRODIGY_AI }}

    steps:
      # Generate prod-igy installation token if GitHub App credentials exist
      - name: Generate prod-igy token
        id: app-token
        if: ${{ env.HAS_APP_ID != '' && env.HAS_PRIVATE_KEY != '' }}
        # continue-on-error: this step is the one place a credential problem can
        # cost the PR its labels and its rebase warning. The GITHUB_TOKEN
        # fallback below already handles an absent token; a *failed* mint has to
        # reach it too, not abort the job.
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1  # v3.2.0
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.PRODIGY_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.PRODIGY_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          # Scope the minted token down from the App's full installation grant to
          # what this job actually does -- an app token otherwise inherits every
          # permission the installation has, regardless of what the job declares.
          #
          # `permission-*` requests that exact set, and the API rejects the whole
          # request with 422 "The permissions requested are not granted to this
          # installation" if even one entry is absent from the installation's
          # grant -- so a well-meant extra mints nothing at all rather than a
          # slightly wider token, and the job silently falls back to
          # github-actions[bot]. This list may therefore only name permissions
          # prod-igy is *installed* with. Probed one permission per token request
          # (actions/runs/36200243473):
          #
          #   granted: pull_requests: write, contents: read, metadata: read
          #   absent:  issues, checks
          #
          # `permission-issues: write` and `permission-checks: read` were both
          # here and both 422'd. Nothing is lost by dropping them: for a *pull
          # request*, GitHub accepts `pull_requests: write` on the issue-comment
          # and label endpoints prod-igy.js uses, and the unscoped token this
          # replaced never carried `checks` either -- so the check-run section of
          # the comment has always been running on GITHUB_TOKEN's `checks: read`.
          # Grant the App "Checks: read" if that section should survive a future
          # tightening.
          #
          # The 422 was invisible on pull requests because `pull_request_target`
          # runs the workflow from the *base* branch and main does not carry this
          # block yet: it would have hit every PR the moment develop was promoted.
          # Only a real token request proves a set; re-probe after editing it.
          permission-contents: read
          permission-pull-requests: write

      # The GITHUB_TOKEN fallback below is silent otherwise: a revoked or
      # unconfigured App key means every comment posts as github-actions[bot]
      # with nothing in the run log to say so.
      - name: Report posting identity

name: provenance

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.head_ref || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  PYTHONUNBUFFERED: "1"
  FORCE_COLOR: "1"

jobs:
  reuse:
    name: License & Copyright Compliance (REUSE/SPDX)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1  # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Lint License Headers (reuse)
        id: reuse_lint
        run: pipx run reuse lint

      - name: Generate REUSE License Compliance Step Summary
        if: always()
        shell: bash
        env:
          # Reports the lint's real outcome. Hardcoding "✅ Passed" under
          # `if: always()` rendered a green row in the summary of a run whose
          # lint had just failed.
          LINT: ${{ steps.reuse_lint.outcome }}
        run: |
          if [ "$LINT" = "success" ]; then
            status="✅ Passed"
          else
            status="❌ Failed ($LINT)"
          fi
          # `printf '%s'`, not an unquoted heredoc. The summary now interpolates a
          # variable, and `cat << EOF` (unquoted, as it must be for that) also
          # performs command substitution -- so a single backtick or `$(` added to
          # a table cell later would execute. A quoted `<< 'EOF'` cannot expand
          # `$status` at all, so the table is printed with placeholders instead
          # and nothing in it is ever evaluated.
          {
            printf '### 📜 License & Copyright Compliance (REUSE/SPDX)\n\n'
            printf '| Policy | Status | Standard |\n'
            printf '| :--- | :---: | :--- |\n'
            printf '| **SPDX Header & Licensing** | %s | %s |\n' \
              "$status" "Free Software Foundation Europe (FSFE) REUSE 3.0"
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

  zizmor:
    name: Workflow Security Audit (zizmor)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: read
      security-events: write  # upload SARIF to Code Scanning
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1  # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      # Two passes, because `--format sarif` makes zizmor exit 0 even when it
      # has findings -- verified A/B on this tree at this pinned version:
      # `--format plain` exits 12, `--format sarif` exits 0. Running only the
      # SARIF pass therefore made this job structurally incapable of failing,
      # and a real `self-repository` finding sat unsuppressed behind it. The
      # SARIF pass still runs first and unconditionally so Code Scanning gets
      # the upload even when the gate below fails.
      - name: Audit workflows and the composite action (SARIF for Code Scanning)
        run: |
          pipx run "zizmor==1.30.1" --config .github/zizmor.yml \
            --format sarif . > zizmor.sarif

      - name: Gate on zizmor findings
        id: zizmor_gate
        run: |
          pipx run "zizmor==1.30.1" --config .github/zizmor.yml \
            --format plain .

      - name: Generate Security Audit Step Summary
        if: always()
        shell: bash
        env:
          # Reports what the gate actually did. The previous hardcoded
          # "✅ Passed" was written under `if: always()`, so a failed audit
          # still rendered a green row in the run summary.
          GATE: ${{ steps.zizmor_gate.outcome }}
        run: |
          if [ "$GATE" = "success" ]; then
            status="✅ Passed"
            detail="Zero unmitigated high/medium security anti-patterns"
          else
            status="❌ Failed ($GATE)"
            detail="zizmor reported unsuppressed findings -- see the job log"
          fi
          # printf with placeholders rather than an unquoted heredoc -- see the
          # REUSE summary above for why.

            status="✅ Passed"

            detail="zizmor reported unsuppressed findings -- see the job log"
          fi

          {

name: Publish

# Unified Release Pipeline:
# 1. prepare-release: Bumps version across all files, commits, tags, and validates consistency.
# 2. publish: Tests and publishes to PyPI via OIDC, waits for CDN, then publishes to the MCP Registry.
# 3. release: Creates GitHub Release from CHANGELOG.md and advances the floating major tag (e.g. v1).
#
# workflow_dispatch only, deliberately. prepare-release's own tag push and the
# release job's `gh release create` each used to match this same workflow's
# `push: tags:` / `release: types: [published]` triggers, so every successful
# release re-triggered itself two more times for the same tag. The pypi job
# tolerated the duplicate (skip-existing); mcp-registry does not
# ("cannot publish duplicate version", a hard failure) -- and every extra run
# is pure wasted CI time regardless. One trigger, run by a human, is correct:
# this pipeline already does the tag push and the release creation itself in
# the same run, so there is no separate "release already tagged, now publish"
# case to support.
#
# The release branch is an explicit input, defaulting to `main`, and every
# stage reads it rather than assuming the dispatch ref. That matters because
# workflow_dispatch runs against whatever ref the operator picked in the UI:
# before this input existed, dispatching from `develop` bumped *develop's*
# content but opened the release PR against a hardcoded `main` base, so the
# tag and the published artifact could disagree about what was in them.
# Checking out `inputs.branch` explicitly removes that mismatch -- the branch
# named here is the one that is bumped, merged, tagged and published, whatever
# ref the run was launched from.

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      branch:
        description: >-
          Branch to release from. The version bump is committed against this
          branch, merged into it, and the tag is cut from the merge commit.
          Leave as `main` unless you are deliberately publishing from elsewhere.
        required: false
        default: main
        type: string

concurrency:
  # One release at a time, and NEVER cancelled. Concurrency groups are already
  # scoped to the repository, so a constant group name serialises every run of
  # this workflow -- deliberately not keyed on the branch input, because two
  # dispatches for two different branches are exactly the collision to prevent:
  # each runs bump_version.py, then they race on the tag push and on the PyPI
  # upload. Queueing the second is correct; cancelling a release part-way
  # through an upload is not.
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Stage 1: prepare-release
  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
  prepare-release:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 90
    permissions:
      contents: write
      pull-requests: write
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.version }}
      tag: ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.tag }}
    steps:
      - name: Generate prod-igy token
        id: app-token
        if: ${{ env.HAS_APP_ID != '' && env.HAS_PRIVATE_KEY != '' }}
        uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1  # v3.2.0
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.PRODIGY_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.PRODIGY_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          # Scope the minted token to exactly what this job's own
          # `permissions:` block above allows -- an app token otherwise
          # inherits every permission the installation has.
          permission-contents: write
          permission-pull-requests: write
        env:
          HAS_APP_ID: ${{ secrets.PRODIGY_APP_ID }}
          HAS_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.PRODIGY_PRIVATE_KEY }}

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1  # v7.0.1
        with:
          # The release branch, not the dispatch ref: see the header comment.

          git config user.email "$bot_email"

          # while bump_version.py rewrote more than five, and a --files that
          # misses a path is the worst failure available here: a release commit

          # Asked for, not restated. This list used to be five hand-typed paths
          # while bump_version.py rewrote more than five, and a --files that
          # misses a path is the worst failure available here: a release commit

          # push: a runner-made commit is never marked Verified even when pushed

          # signed commits. An unsigned bump commit here blocks every auto-merge
          # attempt below until someone with branch-protection bypass merges it

          commit_sha=$(python scripts/commit_release_via_api.py \

            --branch "$branch" \
            --base "$RELEASE_BASE" \
            --message "chore(release): bump version to $version" \

          # above via the API; discard them from the local worktree so the
          # `git pull origin "$RELEASE_BASE"` after merge below (which re-fetches
          # the bumped content properly, via the merge) doesn't fail with "local
          # changes would be overwritten".
          git checkout -- "${release_files[@]}"

            echo "=== Attempt $attempt of 30: Checking PR status ==="

            mergeable=$(echo "$pr_info" | jq -r .mergeable)

            if [ "$pr_state" = "MERGED" ]; then

                merged=true
                break

            fi

                echo "Successfully merged $pr_url!"

            if [ "$attempt" -lt 30 ]; then

          # Verify server.json carries ownership marker in README.md

          if ! grep -qF "mcp-name: $name" README.md; then

  # Stage 2: publish (PyPI + MCP Registry)
  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------

    needs: prepare-release
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    environment:
      name: pypi
      url: https://pypi.org/p/repo2graph
    permissions:
      id-token: write        # mints short-lived Trusted Publishing token
      contents: read
    steps:

          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97  # v7.0.0

          python-version: "3.12"

      # a bare `pip install -e ".[dev,mcp]"` resolves whatever PyPI serves at

      # nobody reviewed -- and failing *here* aborts a release that is already
      # tagged and has an open, merged bump commit behind it. That is a worse
      # place to discover upstream drift than a PR run, and `drift` in ci.yml

      # other tool in this file; --locked fails rather than re-resolving if

      - name: Install the locked dependency set
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip
          python -m pip install "uv==0.12.15"

            -o "$RUNNER_TEMP/requirements-publish.txt"
          python -m pip install --require-hashes -r "$RUNNER_TEMP/requirements-publish.txt"
          python -m pip install -e . --no-deps

          python -m pip install --upgrade build

        uses: pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@dc37677b2e1c63e2034f94d8a5b11f265b73ba33  # v1.14.2
        with:
          skip-existing: true
          attestations: true

  mcp-registry:
    needs: [prepare-release, pypi]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      id-token: write        # mcp-publisher login github-oidc needs this
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1  # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.prepare-release.outputs.tag }}
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Wait for PyPI to serve the new version
        env:
          VERSION: ${{ needs.prepare-release.outputs.version }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          for attempt in $(seq 1 30); do
            if curl -sf "https://pypi.org/pypi/repo2graph/$VERSION/json" > /dev/null; then
              echo "repo2graph $VERSION is live on PyPI"
              exit 0
            fi
            echo "attempt $attempt: not visible yet, waiting 10s"
            sleep 10
          done
          echo "::error::repo2graph $VERSION never appeared on PyPI"
          exit 1

      # Pinned by version *and* by digest, like every action SHA in this repo.
      # This was the one unpinned executable here: `releases/latest/download/...`
      # piped straight into `tar xz` and then run in a job holding
      # `id-token: write`, so whatever upstream re-tagged as "latest" got an OIDC
      # identity against the MCP Registry. `latest` is a moving pointer, and a
      # pipe into tar cannot be checked at all -- there is no complete file to
      # hash until after tar has already written the binary.
      #
      # The platform detection went with it: this job is `runs-on:
      # ubuntu-latest`, so `uname` was always `linux`/`x86_64`. Naming the one
      # real target makes the digest below checkable rather than decorative.
      #
      # To bump: read the new digest from that release's
      # `registry_<version>_checksums.txt` and change both values together.
      - name: Install mcp-publisher
        env:
          MCP_PUBLISHER_VERSION: v1.8.1
          MCP_PUBLISHER_SHA256: a06c9096dcb9727c13555b6be26c7effa707b01f06a4c561ba7a3635443cf2cc
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          url="https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/registry/releases/download/${MCP_PUBLISHER_VERSION}/mcp-publisher_linux_amd64.tar.gz"
          curl -fsSL --retry 3 -o mcp-publisher.tar.gz "$url"
          echo "${MCP_PUBLISHER_SHA256}  mcp-publisher.tar.gz" | sha256sum -c -
          tar xzf mcp-publisher.tar.gz mcp-publisher
          rm -f mcp-publisher.tar.gz

      - name: Validate server.json
        run: ./mcp-publisher validate

      - name: Authenticate to the MCP Registry
        run: ./mcp-publisher login github-oidc

      - name: Publish to the MCP Registry
        run: ./mcp-publisher publish

  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Stage 3: release (GitHub Release + Floating Major Tag)
  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------

name: publish.yml
text:
# file: .github/workflows/publish.yml (yml, 516 lines)
        run: ./mcp-publisher login github-oidc

      - name: Publish to the MCP Registry
        run: ./mcp-publisher publish

  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Stage 3: release (GitHub Release + Floating Major Tag)
  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
  release:
    needs: [prepare-release, pypi, mcp-registry]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - name: Generate prod-igy token
        id: app-token
        if: ${{ env.HAS_APP_ID != '' && env.HAS_PRIVATE_KEY != '' }}
        uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1  # v3.2.0
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.PRODIGY_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.PRODIGY_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          # Scope the minted token to exactly what this job's own
          # `permissions:` block above allows -- an app token otherwise
          # inherits every permission the installation has.
          permission-contents: write
        env:
          HAS_APP_ID: ${{ secrets.PRODIGY_APP_ID }}
          HAS_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.PRODIGY_PRIVATE_KEY }}

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1  # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.prepare-release.outputs.tag }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          # persist-credentials stays at its default (true): "Advance floating
          # major tag" further down relies on the credential this checkout
          # persists for the app/GITHUB_TOKEN above.

      - name: Extract this version's CHANGELOG section
        env:
          VERSION: ${{ needs.prepare-release.outputs.version }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          python - <<'PY' > release-notes.md
          import os, re, sys, pathlib
          version = os.environ["VERSION"]
          text = pathlib.Path("CHANGELOG.md").read_text(encoding="utf8")
          pattern = re.compile(
              r"^## \[?" + re.escape(version) + r"\]?.*?$(.*?)(?=^## |\Z)",
              re.M | re.S)
          match = pattern.search(text)
          if not match or not match.group(1).strip():
              print(f"::error::CHANGELOG.md has no section for {version}",
                    file=sys.stderr)
              raise SystemExit(1)
          print(match.group(1).strip())
          PY
          test -s release-notes.md

      - name: Create or update GitHub Release
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || github.token }}
          TAG: ${{ needs.prepare-release.outputs.tag }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if gh release view "$TAG" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo "Release $TAG already exists, updating notes..."
            gh release edit "$TAG" --notes-file release-notes.md
          else
            gh release create "$TAG" --title "$TAG" --notes-file release-notes.md --verify-tag
          fi

      - name: Advance floating major tag
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || github.token }}
          APP_ID: ${{ secrets.PRODIGY_APP_ID }}
          APP_SLUG: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.app-slug }}
          TAG: ${{ needs.prepare-release.outputs.tag }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          major="${TAG%%.*}"
          bot_name="${APP_SLUG:-prod-igy}[bot]"
          if [ -n "${APP_ID:-}" ]; then
            bot_email="${APP_ID}+${bot_name}@users.noreply.github.com"
          else
            bot_email="41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          fi
          git config user.name "$bot_name"
          git config user.email "$bot_email"
          git tag -f "$major" "$TAG"
          git push -f origin "refs/tags/$major"
          echo "Advanced floating tag $major to $TAG" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      - name: Release summary
        env:
          VERSION: ${{ needs.prepare-release.outputs.version }}

name: publish.yml
text:
# file: .github/workflows/publish.yml (yml, 516 lines)
          git config user.email "$bot_email"
          git tag -f "$major" "$TAG"
          git push -f origin "refs/tags/$major"
          echo "Advanced floating tag $major to $TAG" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      - name: Release summary
        env:
          VERSION: ${{ needs.prepare-release.outputs.version }}
          RELEASE_BASE: ${{ inputs.branch }}
        run: |
          {
            echo "### Published and Released repo2graph $VERSION"
            echo
            echo "- **Released from branch**: \`$RELEASE_BASE\`"

            echo "- **MCP Registry**: \`io.github.Srinivasan-78/repo2graph\`"

            echo '```'
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

name: self-index.yml
text:
# file: .github/workflows/self-index.yml (yml, 41 lines)
name: Index this repository

# Keeps a fresh graph of the repository the workflow lives in.
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  schedule:
    - cron: "0 4 * * 1"
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  # The graph only ever reflects the newest commit, so an older in-flight index
  # of a superseded commit is wasted work.
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: write

jobs:
  index:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1  # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0  # full history so CO_CHANGE edges are meaningful
          # The composite action's own push step inits a fresh repo in a temp
          # dir and authenticates via its own `http.extraheader` (github.token,
          # not this checkout's credential), so nothing here depends on the
          # credential actions/checkout would otherwise persist.
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: ./  # the composite action at the repo root
        with:
          path: .
          out: .r2g
          git-history: "500"
          artifact-name: repo-graph
          commit-branch: graph  # drop this line to only publish an artifact

name: zizmor.yml
text:
# file: .github/zizmor.yml (yml, 73 lines)
# zizmor audit configuration (issue #402).
#
# Every ignore below is deliberate and reviewed, not a blanket suppression:
# each entry pins one finding at one file:line, so a new finding of the same
# kind elsewhere in .github/workflows/ still fails the gate. Re-run
# `uvx zizmor --config .github/zizmor.yml .github/workflows/` after any
# workflow edit near these lines -- a shifted line number un-ignores the
# finding rather than silently keeping it suppressed.
rules:
  artipacked:
    ignore:
      # These two checkout steps intentionally rely on the credential
      # actions/checkout persists (default persist-credentials: true) to
      # authenticate a later plain `git push` / `git tag` in the same job --
      # there is no separate credential-routing step to hand it to. Both are
      # scoped to that job's own narrow `permissions:` (or an explicitly-minted,
      # permission-scoped App token) and the job ends immediately after the
      # push, so the persisted credential is never live longer than the push it
      # exists for.
      #
      # `lockfile.yml` used to be a third entry. It is not ignored any more
      # because it no longer needs to be: that checkout now sets
      # `persist-credentials` to an expression that is true only on the
      # dispatch-with-auto_commit path, so the audit is satisfied on the
      # `pull_request` path -- which is the path that never pushes and the one
      # the blanket ignore was wrongly covering. Verified: deleting this entry
      # changes zizmor's output not at all, so keeping it would be dead config
      # that could silently absorb a future real finding if lines shift onto it.
      - publish.yml:85     # prepare-release: `git push origin refs/tags/$tag`
      - publish.yml:435    # release: `git push -f origin refs/tags/$major`

  dangerous-triggers:
    ignore:
      # prod-igy's `pull_request_target` is the documented, narrow exception
      # issue #402 itself asks this audit to surface -- and it does. The
      # mitigations are already in the workflow's own header comment and are
      # test-enforced, not just described: tests/test_prod_igy.py::
      # test_ai_workflow_wiring pins the sparse checkout to exactly
      # `.github/scripts/prod-igy.js` (no PR-head ref reachable),
      # test_iss208_* pin the author_association gate on the one
      # contributor-reachable trigger (issue_comment), and
      # test_ai_workflow_survives_a_registry_outage / the SDK install step's
      # `--ignore-scripts` keep a compromised npm dependency from running
      # lifecycle scripts in this job. Dropping pull_request_target entirely
      # would remove the write-scoped identity prod-igy needs to label PRs
      # and post its inspection comment.
      - prod-igy.yml:16

  self-repository:
    ignore:
      # `uses: ./` referencing this repository's own composite action, from
      # this repository's own workflows -- the pattern the audit flags
      # (an unpinned self-reference) is structurally the point here: these
      # jobs exist to smoke-test the action at the exact commit checked out,
      # not at a separate pinned ref that could drift from what the PR
      # actually changed.
      - ci.yml:317         # action: smoke-tests the composite action itself
      - index-repo.yml:59  # index: dispatch-driven build against a target repo
      - self-index.yml:34  # index: keeps this repo's own graph fresh

  adhoc-packages:
    ignore:
      # `npm install --ignore-scripts '@anthropic-ai/sdk@0.127.0'` in
      # prod-igy.yml has no package.json/lockfile to pin against because this
      # is the only npm dependency `.github/scripts/prod-igy.js` has -- adding
      # a lockfile for one pinned package would be more surface, not less.
      # The version is pinned exactly (not a range), the install happens only
      # when `vars.PRODIGY_AI == 'true'` (opt-in), and `--ignore-scripts`
      # keeps a compromised release from running a lifecycle script in a job
      # that holds pull-requests: write and an API key -- see

name: .pre-commit-config.yaml
text:
# file: .pre-commit-config.yaml (yaml, 62 lines)
#
# Install once with:  pip install pre-commit && pre-commit install
repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff-pre-commit
    rev: v0.14.2
    hooks:
      - id: ruff
        name: ruff check
        args: [--fix, --exit-non-zero-on-fix]
      - id: ruff-format
        name: ruff format --check
        args: [--check]

  - repo: https://github.com/pre-commit/pre-commit-hooks
    rev: v6.0.0
    hooks:
      - id: end-of-file-fixer
      - id: trailing-whitespace
      - id: check-yaml
      - id: check-json
      - id: check-toml
      # The repo declares `* text=auto eol=lf`; this enforces it, because
      # Windows editors still write CRLF and the churn is invisible until
      # someone diffs a file they never edited.
      - id: mixed-line-ending
        args: [--fix=lf]
      - id: check-merge-conflict

  - repo: local
    hooks:
      - id: version-consistency
        name: every version surface must agree with pyproject.toml
        entry: python scripts/check_version.py
        language: system
        pass_filenames: false
        # The file list is scripts/version_surfaces.py's `paths`, plus the table
        # and the two scripts that read it. Narrower than "run always" so an
        # unrelated commit does not pay for it, but it must cover the *documented*
        # surfaces too: a commit that edits only README.md can stale the `@vN`
        # tag, and the old regex named three files and would not have fired.
        files: >-
          ^(pyproject\.toml|server\.json|uv\.lock|repo2graph/__init__\.py|README\.md|\.github/SECURITY\.md|docs/(github-action|ACTION_SECURITY|SECURITY-AUDIT|ENTERPRISE_DEPLOYMENT)\.md|scripts/(version_surfaces|check_version|bump_version)\.py)$

      - id: mypy-strict
        # Strict, and green, on the modules that are annotated. The legacy
        # modules carry the remaining annotation debt; a hook that is red on
        # every commit gets disabled within a week, so they are relaxed in
        # pyproject and the debt is tracked in docs/BACKLOG.md instead of pretended away.
        #
        # The scope lives in pyproject's [[tool.mypy.overrides]] and nowhere
        # else. This used to restate it as a regex of six module names, which
        # inverted the stated intent: a brand-new module matched neither the
        # override nor the regex, so it was strict "by default" and checked by
        # nothing. Matching the whole package defers to pyproject, so removing a
        # module from the override list is the single edit that tightens it.
        name: mypy --strict (annotated modules)
        entry: python -m mypy
        language: system
        types: [python]
        files: ^repo2graph/.*\.py$
        require_serial: true

name: AGENTS.md
text:
# file: AGENTS.md (md, 210 lines)
# Repo rules

## Text slicing — use `split("\n")`, never `splitlines()`

tree-sitter advances `Point.row` on `\n` only. `str.splitlines()` (and universal-newline mode)
*also* break on U+2028, U+2029, U+0085, `\x0b` and `\x0c` — so any source file containing one of
those desyncs Python's line list from the parser's row numbers, and every later symbol's chunk
text gets sliced from the wrong lines. This bug class keeps recurring: ISS-22 (`chunks.py`) and the
`query.py` comment near its `read_jsonl`. The git-log instance this rule used to call "still-open
at `graph.py:380`" is closed — that call is now `split("\n")` with the reason inline — and there
are **no `.splitlines()` calls left anywhere in `repo2graph/`**. Keep it that way; the three
remaining matches for the word are this rule being cited in prose.

- Slice source-against-parser with `src.split("\n")`, dropping a trailing `"\r"` per line for CRLF.
- `chunks.py` already has a `_lines(src)` helper that does exactly this — reuse it.
- `splitlines()` is fine only on content that is guaranteed `\n`-only (e.g. `graph.py:162`
  reading `go.mod`).

## Decoding git subprocess output (Windows / non-UTF-8 locales)

Never pass `text=True` (or `encoding=<locale>`) to a `subprocess` call that reads **git** output.
The Windows locale is cp1252, so a non-ASCII path raises `UnicodeDecodeError` — sometimes inside
the error handler, masking the real failure. Every historical regression in this repo is a
Windows encoding bug (ISS-06/17/22/27); CI now has a `windows-latest` leg specifically to catch
the class.

The established pattern — originated in `walker._git_files`, now also in `graph.add_cochange`
and `fetch.py`:

- run git with `-c core.quotepath=false` so non-ASCII paths return raw, not `"caf\303\251.py"`
  (the quoted form never matches a path/file index, so edges silently vanish);
- capture bytes and `.decode("utf8", "surrogateescape")`;
- always set `timeout=` and convert `TimeoutExpired` into that call's normal error type;
- `fetch.py` may instead use `encoding="utf8", errors="replace"` for user-facing text — same
  intent, no crash on a stray byte.

## Discovery indexes dot-directories, git or not

`walker.discover()` applies one `DEFAULT_SKIP_DIRS` filter to both sources (`git ls-files` and
the `os.walk` fallback) — ISS-13. The `os.walk` path no longer drops every dot-directory, so a
plain-folder build now indexes `.github/**` and any dot-dir not in `DEFAULT_SKIP_DIRS`, matching
what a git checkout always did. Consequence: on non-git builds, tool caches like `.ruff_cache/`,
`.eggs/`, `.cache/` are picked up unless their names are added to `DEFAULT_SKIP_DIRS`
(open follow-up SH-5).

## Two budget models coexist — do not unify them

`Index.retrieve()` and `Index.pack_context()` mean different things by `budget_chars`, on purpose.
`retrieve()` (`query.py:272`) bounds the sum of the returned chunks' `text` only; `pack_context()`
(`query.py:349`) bounds the **whole returned markdown** — map prepend, the `---` separator, every
`### [cite: ...]` header and the blank lines between blocks all charge against it. This reads like
an inconsistency and it is not one: `retrieve()`'s text-only accounting is pinned by
`tests/test_repo2graph.py` (`test_index_retrieves_and_expands`,
`test_iss25_query_constants_and_budget_bounds`) and consumed by `cmd_query`, so "harmonising" the
two silently changes `repo2graph query`'s output for every existing caller.

- New retrieval surface goes on `pack_context()`. `retrieve()` is a back-compat surface: keep its
  positional order `(query, k, hops, budget_chars)` and add only keyword-only params that default
  to today's behaviour (`min_confidence=None` means "no confidence filter", which is what the
  pre-GraphRAG code did).
- `pack_context(budget_chars <= 0)` is unbounded; `retrieve()` has no such convention.

## A new default on a shared traversal helper narrows its existing callers

When you add a filtering parameter to a helper that already has callers, the *safe* default for

# file: AGENTS.md (md, 210 lines)
  positional order `(query, k, hops, budget_chars)` and add only keyword-only params that default
  to today's behaviour (`min_confidence=None` means "no confidence filter", which is what the
  pre-GraphRAG code did).
- `pack_context(budget_chars <= 0)` is unbounded; `retrieve()` has no such convention.

## A new default on a shared traversal helper narrows its existing callers

When you add a filtering parameter to a helper that already has callers, the *safe* default for
the helper is not the safe default for the callers. `expand()` gained
`edge_dirs=None → DEFAULT_EDGE_DIRS` (`query.py:36,245`) — `DEFINES: ("in",)`, `IMPORTS: ("out",)`,
`INHERITS: ("out",)` — which the new packing path wants. `retrieve()` passed no `edge_dirs`, so it
inherited the narrowing and silently lost every DEFINES-out, IMPORTS-in and INHERITS-in neighbour
(41 → 28 neighbours on one probe query; `repo2graph query "how does export write manifest"` dropped
`sym:repo2graph/export.py::_flat`). Same shape as the confidence gate, which *was* neutralised.

- Every pre-existing caller must opt out **by name**, not by omission. `ALL_EDGE_DIRS: dict = {}`
  (`query.py:48`) exists solely so `retrieve()` (`query.py:302-307`) says "no direction filter" in
  the source, where a reader and a `grep` can both see it.
- The confidence gate is `CALLS`-only by design: IMPORTS / DEFINES / INHERITS records carry no
  `confidence` key, and `min_confidence` must never drop them.
- Prove the neutrality against the **baseline**, not against the new code: `git worktree add <tmp>
  <baseline-sha>`, run the same seed list through both trees, compare the tuple lists.

## Tests must pin values, not compare the implementation to itself

`cmd_query`'s output test asserted stdout `== format_pack(Index(out).retrieve(...))`. Both sides
move together under any traversal change, so it stayed green straight through the narrowing bug
above and would stay green through the next one. Same shape in `tests/test_rag.py`'s
`compressed_form` helper, which re-implements `query._compress` and then asserts they agree.

- For retrieval/traversal behaviour, assert literal `(node_id, why)` membership hand-derived from
  the fixture source — never a value computed by the code under test. Set membership only; no
  score, rank, float or ordering (those drift with any scoring tweak).
- Prove a new test is a detector: revert the fix in the working copy, watch the new test fail and
  the old one pass, then restore and confirm `git hash-object` is unchanged.

## A file with little residue emits no file-level chunk

`chunks.py:185` drops a `file_residual` chunk whose body is under 40 characters after every symbol
span is carved out. So a small module that is *all* imports and defs has a node but no chunk — and
a node with no chunk can be neither a seed nor a retrievable neighbour. Consequence for fixtures:
a synthetic package whose modules are pure `def`s physically cannot express an IMPORTS edge through
`retrieve()`, no matter what the traversal does. Give each module a module-level constant/table so
its file node carries a chunk (the `dirs_out` fixture in `tests/test_rag.py` exists only for this;
`rag_repo` hits the threshold and was left alone).

## `layout.path(out, "overview.md")` is `human/overview.md`, not `agent/`

`overview.md` is the one artifact written to two sections — `SECTIONS["overview.md"] = (HUMAN_DIR,
AGENT_DIR)` (`layout.py:45`) — and `layout.rel()` returns the **first**, so `path()` resolves to
`human/`. Everything else agent-facing resolves to `agent/`, which makes the wrong assumption easy.
Readers that must tolerate a deleted overview should treat either copy as optional; use
`layout.paths()` when you need both.

## `rag --answer` uploads repository source to a third-party endpoint

`repo2graph rag --answer` POSTs the assembled pack — real file content out of `chunks.jsonl` — to
whichever provider wins the `GEMINI_API_KEY` → `OPENAI_API_KEY` → `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` →
`OLLAMA_HOST` precedence race. Non-source files are chunked whole, so a `.env` in the indexed repo

# file: AGENTS.md (md, 210 lines)
Readers that must tolerate a deleted overview should treat either copy as optional; use
`layout.paths()` when you need both.

## `rag --answer` uploads repository source to a third-party endpoint

`repo2graph rag --answer` POSTs the assembled pack — real file content out of `chunks.jsonl` — to
whichever provider wins the `GEMINI_API_KEY` → `OPENAI_API_KEY` → `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` →
`OLLAMA_HOST` precedence race. Non-source files are chunked whole, so a `.env` in the indexed repo
can be seeded by a query and shipped verbatim. Treat this as the sensitive path:

- It is gated: `answer` is imported lazily and only under `if args.answer:`; a plain `rag` makes no
  DNS lookup and no connect. Keep it that way, and keep the socket-level no-network test.
- `answer._disclose()` prints provider + **hostname only** to stderr before the first byte. Never
  put a credential in a URL (the Gemini key moved to the `x-goog-api-key` header for exactly this
  reason) and never echo `HTTPError.url` in an error message.
- Closed: a `--provider` flag forces a specific provider, and dotfile/secret-ish paths are
  excluded from every `rag`/`query` result -- `--answer` or not -- unless `--include-secrets` is
  passed *at query time* (a build-time `--include-secrets` no longer leaks into later reads).

## Vectors are keyed by chunk id on disk and by list index in memory

`score_rrf(vectors=...)` indexes by the chunk's position in `self.chunks` (`vectors[i] for i in
candidates`), but positions move whenever `chunks.jsonl` is rebuilt. So `vectors.npy` /
`vectors.meta.json` persist `chunk_ids` in row order and `Index.__init__` translates id → current
list index at load. Persisting by row index instead would "work" until the first rebuild that
reorders chunks and then mis-rank silently, forever.

- A missing, truncated or malformed vector pair must leave `self.vectors = None` and raise nothing —
  BM25 is always the floor. Same for ids `chunks.jsonl` no longer contains: they are dropped.
- **Never default the query-side embedding model to `vector_meta["model_id"]`.** `fuse_ok` exists to
  catch a model mismatch; feeding it the index's own model id on both sides makes it a comparison of
  a value with itself — permanently true, unfalsifiable, and the guard is gone. `--embed-model`
  defaults to `embed.DEFAULT_MODEL`, never to what the index happens to claim.
- `embed.py`'s `.npy` reader/writer is stdlib-only **by design**, not for lack of effort. A machine
  that only *queries* a shipped index must not need numpy, or the zero-dependency promise breaks for
  exactly the case vectors were added for. numpy is a fast path when importable, never a requirement.

## Every MCP tool argument is caller-hostile

`repo2graph/mcp.py` hands its output straight into an agent's context window, and the caller picks
the arguments. Bounds go in the **handler**, not in `serve()`, so direct callers, `dispatch()` and
the stdio server all inherit them — this was missed twice in one run (`hops`/`k` first, then
`limit`), each time producing a tool that could return tens of thousands of characters.

- Any new numeric tool argument goes through `_clamp` against an `MCP_MAX_*` constant, in the
  handler, and gets a test that floods the fixture until the ceiling actually binds. A bound asserted
  against a 4-neighbour fixture proves nothing.
- All three handlers pass `exclude_secrets=True` unconditionally. A human running the CLI chose to
  see `.env`; an agent tool returning it is a different class of problem.

## `action.yml`: GitHub expressions and shell disagree about truthiness

GitHub's expression language compares strings **case-insensitively**, so `if: inputs.embed ==
'true'` fires for `"True"` and `"TRUE"`. POSIX `[ "$X" = "true" ]` does not. An input gated in both
places therefore has a casing where the first gate opens and the second stays shut — here that meant
the embed step ran and the rag step then dropped `--vectors`, computing vectors and ignoring them.
The Python suite cannot see this at all.

# file: AGENTS.md (md, 210 lines)

## `action.yml`: GitHub expressions and shell disagree about truthiness

GitHub's expression language compares strings **case-insensitively**, so `if: inputs.embed ==
'true'` fires for `"True"` and `"TRUE"`. POSIX `[ "$X" = "true" ]` does not. An input gated in both
places therefore has a casing where the first gate opens and the second stays shut — here that meant
the embed step ran and the rag step then dropped `--vectors`, computing vectors and ignoring them.
The Python suite cannot see this at all.

- Case-fold in the shell (`tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]'`); the expression language has no
  case-sensitive compare, so tightening the `if:` is not an option.
- `-n` / `-z` non-emptiness tests agree with GitHub for every casing — only `==` equality gates need
  this. `tests/test_compat.py`'s R-6 executes the real `run:` body across casings and fails if a new
  `inputs.X ==` gate appears.

## Discovery order *is* artifact order — keep `discover()` sorted

Node ids are emitted as files are parsed, and edges and chunks follow the nodes. So anything that
perturbs discovery order perturbs `nodes.jsonl`, `edges.jsonl` and `chunks.jsonl` byte-for-byte
while describing an identical graph. `git ls-files` happens to sort; `os.walk` returns filesystem
order — alphabetical on NTFS, hash order on ext4 with `dir_index` — so a non-git build produced
different artifacts on different machines, and **no same-machine A/B could see it** (on NTFS the
unsorted and sorted orders coincide).

- `discover()` sorts both sources in one place, keyed on `Path.as_posix()`. Not `str(Path)`: that
  sorts on `\` on Windows and `/` elsewhere, which is the same divergence one level down.
- A third discovery source must inherit that sort rather than add its own.
- `--max-files N` takes the first N *in discovery order*, so unsorted discovery made two machines
  index different **subsets** of one tree.
- `tests/test_determinism.py` reverses `os.walk` to stand in for "a different filesystem". A test
  that does not do that is not a detector for this class.

## Every edge carries `method`, `confidence` and `evidence` — normalise at the chokepoint

An edge is a claim about the code; without evidence it is an assertion. Four of the six edge types
were once bare `(src, dst, type)` triples, so "why do you think this file imports that one" had no
answer in the artifact.

- `Graph.add_edge` is the single chokepoint and runs `edgemeta.normalize`, so a **new edge type
  cannot ship without the standard fields**. Add per-type metadata at the call site; never bypass
  `add_edge`.
- `confidence` means P(`dst` is the correct target | the relationship at `evidence` exists) — not
  P(the relationship exists). That separation is why an ambiguous name splits 1/n across candidates
  while the call site stays certain, and why `CALLS_EXTERNAL` is 1.0. It **never** encodes dynamic
  dispatch; `call_kind` does.
- `evidence: null` is a real answer for `CONTAINS` and `CO_CHANGE`. Inventing a line for either
  would be a fabricated citation, which is the failure the field exists to prevent.
- Anything added to `ParsedFile` for evidence must round-trip through `parse.cache.json` **and**
  bump `PARSE_CACHE_FORMAT`, or an incremental build emits edges with no evidence where a full
  build emits a line. `import_lines` was caught by the byte-equality tests doing exactly that.
- `docs/reference.md` and `docs/OUTPUT_SCHEMA.md` both describe these records.
  `tests/test_doc_consistency.py` fails if they disagree.

# file: CHANGELOG.md (md, 1467 lines)
# Changelog

All notable changes to this project are documented here.

The format follows [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/), and
this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

Entries for v1.0.0 through v1.4.0 were reconstructed from git history and the
published GitHub Releases after the fact, so they summarise what shipped rather
than being contemporaneous notes. `.github/workflows/publish.yml` now reads the
section for a version out of this file and uses it as the Release body, which
makes keeping it current a release-blocking step rather than a good intention.

## [Unreleased]

### Added

- **Four new MCP tools**, taking the surface from six to ten
  ([#384](https://github.com/Srinivasan-78/repo2graph/issues/384),
  [#385](https://github.com/Srinivasan-78/repo2graph/issues/385),
  [#386](https://github.com/Srinivasan-78/repo2graph/issues/386),
  [#387](https://github.com/Srinivasan-78/repo2graph/issues/387)):
  - `repo_find_symbol` — name to `node_id`, so an agent that already knows a function name (from a
    traceback, a review comment, the user's question) no longer has to spend a budgeted
    `repo_search` round trip purely to learn an id format. Matches exactly, then
    case-insensitively, then on the last `qualname` segment.
  - `repo_read` — widen a `[cite: path:start-end]` window. Reads from `chunks.jsonl`, **never from
    disk**: chunks have already passed secret-path exclusion and content redaction, and over HTTP
    the client cannot open the path a citation names anyway. `file_residual` chunks concatenate
    non-contiguous spans, so a read covered only by one answers "not indexed" rather than
    returning the wrong lines.
  - `repo_path_between` — bounded bidirectional BFS over the existing adjacency, reporting each
    path's minimum edge confidence. `CO_CHANGE` is opt-in, never traversed by default.
  - `repo_blast_radius` — reverse reachability: the reverse `CALLS` closure by hop distance,
    reverse `INHERITS`, reverse `IMPORTS` on the containing file, and `CO_CHANGE` files by count.
    Named `repo_blast_radius`, not `repo_impact` as issue #387 proposed, because `repo_impact`
    already exists and analyses a PR diff — a different question.
- **MCP server flags for the HTTP transport's new limits**: `--http-insecure-ok`, `--trust-proxy`,
  `--trusted-proxies`, and `--rate-limit-requests` / `--rate-limit-window` /
  `--max-concurrent-requests` / `--max-queue-size` / `--max-concurrent-builds` /
  `--max-response-bytes`. A `RateLimitConfig` is built only when at least one is passed, so
  untouched fields keep their single set of defaults rather than a second, driftable copy.

### Security

- **Rate limiting and concurrency quotas for HTTP MCP**
  ([#264](https://github.com/Srinivasan-78/repo2graph/issues/264)): a per-client sliding window,
  a server-wide concurrency semaphore with a bounded queue and bounded wait, an independent
  build-concurrency gate, and a response-size cap. Client identity comes from the verified auth
  subject where there is one, so a shared bearer token does not pool every caller into one bucket.
  Overload answers in the JSON-RPC implementation-defined error range, not as a malformed-request
  error. The limiter's own identity map is bounded by `max_tracked_clients` — its own knob, since
  eviction from it is not a throttle: it clears a client's history and grants a fresh allowance.
- **Content type is validated on `POST`**
  ([#293](https://github.com/Srinivasan-78/repo2graph/issues/293)): `application/json` with
  optional parameters, case-insensitively. A *missing* Content-Type is refused rather than assumed
  — `urllib` silently sends `x-www-form-urlencoded` when a caller sets no header, which is exactly
  the misconfigured client this check exists to catch.
- **Strict JSON-RPC envelope validation**
  ([#293](https://github.com/Srinivasan-78/repo2graph/issues/293)): `jsonrpc` version, method type
  and length, id type and numeric range, params schema, body length, nesting depth, duplicate

# file: CHANGELOG.md (md, 1467 lines)
- **Content type is validated on `POST`**
  ([#293](https://github.com/Srinivasan-78/repo2graph/issues/293)): `application/json` with
  optional parameters, case-insensitively. A *missing* Content-Type is refused rather than assumed
  — `urllib` silently sends `x-www-form-urlencoded` when a caller sets no header, which is exactly
  the misconfigured client this check exists to catch.
- **Strict JSON-RPC envelope validation**
  ([#293](https://github.com/Srinivasan-78/repo2graph/issues/293)): `jsonrpc` version, method type
  and length, id type and numeric range, params schema, body length, nesting depth, duplicate
  top-level keys, non-finite JSON constants, and strict UTF-8 decoding. Errors are bounded and
  structured; no stack trace reaches a caller.
- **TLS and trusted-proxy rules for remote binds**
  ([#267](https://github.com/Srinivasan-78/repo2graph/issues/267)): binding non-loopback with
  authentication configured prints a high-visibility banner and emits an
  `http_transport_no_tls_termination` event unless explicitly acknowledged — this server does not
  terminate TLS, so a bearer credential travels in clear without a proxy in front of it.
  `X-Forwarded-For` is ignored by default and consulted only when `--trust-proxy` is set *and* the
  immediate peer is in the allowlist, and never for authentication.
- **`Host` and `Origin` are checked on `GET` and `HEAD`**, not only `POST`
  ([#372](https://github.com/Srinivasan-78/repo2graph/issues/372)), so a page in the user's browser
  cannot read the discovery documents or `/healthz` cross-origin. Those stay unauthenticated by
  necessity — a client must learn how to authenticate before it holds a credential.
- **RSA keys below 2048 bits, and unbounded public exponents, fail verification**
  ([#367](https://github.com/Srinivasan-78/repo2graph/issues/367)). Both fail closed exactly as a
  bad signature does, so a caller cannot tell a weak key from a forged one.
- **JSONL index reads are bounded on the untrusted-index path**
  ([#408](https://github.com/Srinivasan-78/repo2graph/issues/408)). An index is untrusted input —
  shipped on a `graph` branch, as Action artifacts and in `examples/`. Lines are framed over fixed
  blocks rather than by `for line in fh`, which reads until a newline and so allocates a
  newline-less file whole *before* any per-line ceiling could measure it; peak memory is now the
  ceiling plus one block. A total-bytes ceiling applies to the verification path
  (`integrity`, `doctor`) only — `chunks.jsonl` is the repository's own text and is legitimately
  large on a monorepo, so a wrong constant there would break real indexes on the `query` path.

- **Terraform state and vendor credential files are secret paths.** `*.tfstate`,
  `*.tfstate.backup`, `*.tfvars` (and `.auto.tfvars`, `.tfvars.json`), `htpasswd`, `wp-config.php`,
  `credentials.yml.enc`, `key.json`, Firebase `*adminsdk*` keys and `auth.json` (except under a
  `locales`/`i18n`/`lang`/`translations`/`messages` directory) are no longer indexed. JSON,
  single-quoted dict and YAML `"password": "..."`-style pairs are redacted in chunk text; values
  containing `://` and keys such as `tokenUrl`, `secretName`, `passwordField` are left alone.
- **`--include-secrets` no longer disables content redaction.** It lifts the secret-*path*
  refusal only; chunk text is still scanned per `--secret-policy` (default `redact-match`).
  Agent-path reads (MCP, `rag --answer`) of an index built with `--secret-policy off`/`warn-only`
  are redacted at serve time.
- **Secret-looking paths are excluded by default everywhere a human reads results**: `rag`,
  `query`, `explain retrieval` and `impact` (previously only MCP and `rag --answer`).
  `--include-secrets` opts back in per command; `--exclude-secrets` is a deprecated no-op.
- **A deeply nested JWT header gets a 401** and an `auth_rejected` audit record instead of an
  escaped `RecursionError` and a dropped connection.
- **`events.emit` fails closed**: if the sanitiser itself raises, field values are dropped
